warnings: SEGMENT-SPLITTING CONVENTION USED HERE, stated because §5 could be read two ways on this sheet. A beam is split at an intersection where a support actually exists on THIS floor - a column, or a beam that visibly crosses it - not at every dummy grid line the master carries. Several dummy lines in the master (1'' 1.70, 3' 6.00) exist only on the upper floor and correctly split nothing here. Where a segment ends on a crossing beam rather than a column it carries the §5 flag bears_on_beam:<mark>(<end>).

NO BEAM RUNS ALONG ง BETWEEN GRIDS 2 AND 4, AND THIS WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. The C2/C2/C1 columns at ง2/ง3/ง4 stand with no beam on the ง line between them; the frame at that end of the house is carried by the B2A pair one line north, on ง''' (-0.80). Checked by scanning the two bays for horizontal dark runs at the ง ordinate - bay 1-2 returns the B2 beam, bays 2-3 and 3-4 return nothing at that ordinate while correctly returning ง''' and ค. The same check confirms there is NO beam on ข between grids 3 and 4 either; that area is the rear terrace SG slab poured on grade.

B3A's MARK IS LEADERED, NOT WRITTEN ON THE LINE. On the ง' line the label B3A sits below the beam with a dashed leader instead of being written along it, the only beam on this sheet labelled that way. The two ง' segments are recorded as B3A on that leader; flagged on both occurrences.

THE REAR SERVICE STRIP (grid 4 to 4') IS THE WEAKEST PART OF THIS EXTRACTION. It is a ~0.60 m wide strip east of grid 4 running from about ค' down past ข, holding several short B1 beams and (S) slab panels. Its internal levels are dimensioned only locally - 0.60, 1.00 and 0.30 appear beside it - and at 1:100 on a reduced booklet scan the individual segment boundaries could not be separated with confidence. Four B1 segments and two (S) panels are recorded with the endpoints that could be resolved, every one flagged rear_service_strip_segmentation_not_fully_resolved. There may be one or two more short segments in it. Nothing was invented to fill the gap and nothing was dropped; a later pass with the original full-size sheet should re-read this strip specifically. The printed 1.00 there implies a line at ข-1.00 (6.00) which is NOT in the grid master, because no beam could be positively read on it.

THE TWO 45° BAY-WINDOW CORNERS. The west wall steps out to 1' between ค and ค'' on two 45° cuts. Their spans are recorded as the hypotenuse of the 0.80 x 0.80 offset (1.13 m), computed from grid positions only, per §4's rule that a span is never model-estimated. The sheet prints 0.65 at both corners, which scales to the OUTER face of the same cut - see the grid master's dimension-convention warning. Flagged on both segments.

SG ON THIS PLAN IS RECORDED AS GS, AND THIS IS A DECISION, NOT A TRANSCRIPTION. Four slab bubbles on the rear terrace and the carport carry a two-letter mark that reads as SG on two of them and GS on the other two at the largest magnification this scan supports; the glyphs are ~10 px tall and S/G are the confusable pair §10 warns about. S-03 (แบบขยายการเสริมเหล็ก ฐานราก,ตอม่อ,เสา พื้น) details exactly five slab marks - S, S1, S2, S3 and GS - and no SG anywhere. Per §7 the detail sheet wins over the plan, and recording a phantom SG would create a mark that can never join to a spec, which is worse than normalising. All four are therefore recorded as GS with the plan reading preserved in element_id_printed_as and flagged. Both are slabs on grade (rear terrace and carport), which is exactly what S-03's GS detail draws, so one mark covering both is physically consistent. A later pass on the full-size sheet should confirm.

SLAB MARKS ON THIS SHEET ARE S, S2, SG AND GS. SG and GS are two different marks, not a transcription of one: SG labels the two rear terrace panels poured on grade inside the building footprint, GS labels the carport slab outside grid 4. Both spellings were re-read at high magnification specifically because of the §10 SI-versus-S1 warning. No S1 and no SI appears anywhere on the ground floor; S1 does appear on the upper floor (S-02).

Slab panels have no beam endpoints of their own, so per §0.8 they carry a single approximate grid_ref (or an area ref) rather than start/end refs, and per §4's ordering rule they are listed after the positioned elements.

SPECS ARE NOT JOINED INTO THIS FILE. Beam sections and reinforcement for B1/B2/B2A/B2B/B2C/B3/B3A/B3B/B3C live on S-04 (หน้า23) and column/pedestal/footing details on S-03 (หน้า22); per §7 they belong in a specs{} object keyed by element_id. They are recorded on those sheets' own files instead of being duplicated here.
